newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Generale Bank 1-for-10 cap increase starts Sept 19.
newsitem.headline: Generale Bank 1-for-10 cap increase starts Sept 19.

text.p: Generale Bank NV, Belgium's biggest bank, said in a statement on Tuesday it plans to make a capital increase in the proportion of one new share for ten existing shares.
On the basis of the share price on September 9, this means an increase of approximately 15 billion Belgian francs.
The issue will run from September 19 to October 4 and will be priced on September 18, chief executive office Ferdinand Chaffart told a news conference.
Chaffart also said the issue price would be based on the bank's share price between September 10 and 18, minus a discount of seven to 12 percent.
The new shares will have the right to dividend as from January 1, 1996.
"The capital increase is neccessary to increase our flexibility and solvency," Chaffart said.
"It will make it possible for us to both take advantage of the acceleration in economic growth in those countries where we are active, and also to continue to pursue our strategy," he added.
Chaffart said, reiterating earlier statements, that Generale Bank is still interested in acquiring a bank in the German state of North-Rhine-Westphalia.

He also said that, as far as priority activities are concerned, the bank is continuing to develop asset management, private banking and financial markets to diversify its income and offset the pressure on the interest margin.
